scope: CPU-only development diagnostic of a frozen initial catalog and saved D19 development rankings; no model change, training, or final-user evaluation.
conclusion: Uniform probability over category branches has a severe initial small-group bias. The trained checkpoint's exact rankings are not dominated by tiny groups, so this does not explain the whole quality deficit. No cardinality-prior variant was implemented.
catalog_semantics: Start from D1-D18 catalog; choose 200k or 1M videos by development-user initial exposure count, ties by raw item ID; store selected IDs in ascending order. Video categories are frozen at earliest initial-window observation. Pair=(c1,c2); category-2 alone is not a unique parent-child path.

protocol.training_request_panel: Same deterministic 50,000 D1-D18 positive-request sample for both catalog sizes. Requests with no in-catalog positive are excluded from these training NLL summaries. Average known-positive NLL within each request, then average requests.
protocol.saved_exact_rankings: 16 fixed D19 requests from the FP32 all-pairs panel; 1,600 ranked video occurrences.
protocol.observed_positive_comparison: 652 in-catalog positive occurrences among the original 1,024 D19 development requests. The paired 16-request panel has only 12 known positives.
protocol.zero_residual_definition: All learned logits equal zero. Let A be number of c1 categories, B(c1) the number of valid c2 children, n(c1,c2) the leaf count. Baseline p(i)=1/[A*B(c1)*n(c1,c2)].
protocol.hypothetical_cardinality_base_measure: Add log(sum_c2 n(c1,c2)) to c1 logits and log(n(c1,c2)) to conditional c2 logits. With zero residual leaf logits this telescopes to p(i)=1/N. This is a label-free initialization/base-measure proposal only, not measured trained-model quality.

catalog_1m.interpretation: The approximately 17 versus 13.8 initial NLL difference is explained by the zero-residual base measure for this request panel; actual randomly initialized logits need not equal these values.

trained_beam100_top100.interpretation: Beam pruning favors high-mass branches and hides smaller branches; this is separate from learned-model quality.
